spans.s: gaurī-paṭṭa, same as the yoni-paṭṭa of a Śiva-liṅga.

gaurī-varāṭikā, ‘virgin-money’. Gaurī means ‘a virgin’ and varāṭikā is used primarily in the sense of varāṭa or varāṭaka, ‘a cowrie-shell’, and secondarily in that of ‘money’. In the records of Mithilā, gaurī-varāṭikā means ‘money to be paid to the master of a slave girl of marriageable age by the master of her bridegroom’. See JNSI, Vol. XVI, pp. 264 ff.
